title: Tech Mahindra Moves to Lift Pininfarina Stake to 92.59% in €9.46 Million Tender
excerpt: PF Holdings has committed to buy 7.886 million more shares at €1.20 each — the step that would cross the 90% line for delisting the Italian design house from Milan.
body:
• Tech Mahindra said on November 6 that its subsidiary PF Holdings B.V. has committed to buy 7,886,000 Pininfarina shares for up to €9.46 million, at €1.20 per share in cash.
  • The block is 10.02% of Pininfarina's issued shares and would lift PF Holdings' stake from 82.57% to 92.59% if the transaction completes.
  • The purchase is part of a voluntary tender offer for up to 13,700,787 shares (17.42%) under Italy's CONSOB rules, as Pininfarina pursues delisting from Borsa Italiana.
  • Completion needs approval from Italy's Presidency of the Council of Ministers, with an indicative close on or before December 31, 2026 — the 92.59% figure is a post-completion outcome, not the current holding.

Tech Mahindra is tightening its grip on Pininfarina, the Italian design house it already controls. In a regulatory filing on November 6, the company said its subsidiary PF Holdings B.V. (PFH) has entered a commitment to tender, signed on November 5, to buy 7,886,000 ordinary shares of Pininfarina S.p.A. for up to €9.46 million — €1.20 per share, in cash. The block equals 10.02% of Pininfarina's issued shares and would take PFH's holding from 82.57% to 92.59%, according to the filing as reported by Dealroom and Multibagg's summary of the disclosure.

The tender behind the commitment

The committed block forms part of a wider voluntary totalitarian tender offer PFH has launched for up to 13,700,787 Pininfarina ordinary shares, or 17.42% of the issued capital, run under the regulations of CONSOB, Italy's market regulator, and exclusively in Italy, where Pininfarina trades on Euronext Milan. Tech Mahindra said the consideration is cash rather than a share swap, and that the transaction is not a related-party transaction. Pininfarina reported consolidated turnover of US$128.7 million for the year ended December 31, 2025.

Why 92.59% matters more than €9.46 million

By value, €9.46 million is a small transaction for a company of Tech Mahindra's size. Its significance is the threshold it crosses. Tech Mahindra said Pininfarina is pursuing a delisting from Borsa Italiana, subject to applicable laws and regulations, and crossing 90% ownership is the stated threshold to take the company private. The committed purchase, if it completes, puts PFH above that line at 92.59% — folding the design house fully into the Mahindra group and removing it from public markets.

How PF Holdings got here

PF Holdings is the Dutch vehicle through which Tech Mahindra and Mahindra & Mahindra bought control of Pininfarina in 2015-16, held 60% by Tech Mahindra and 40% by Mahindra & Mahindra. The march toward a take-private has been running all autumn: in September, Reuters reported that PF Holdings, then holding about 78.8% of Pininfarina, had launched a voluntary tender offer for up to 16.7 million further shares — 21.2% of the company — at €1 per share, with the stated aim of delisting Pininfarina from Euronext Milan. The stake has since risen to the current 82.57%, and this week's commitment, at a higher €1.20 per share, is the step designed to carry it past 90%.

What still has to happen

The stake increase is not done yet. Completion requires approval from the Presidency of the Council of Ministers in Italy, and the filing gives an indicative completion date on or before December 31, 2026. Until then, PFH's holding remains the current 82.57%, and the delisting itself remains subject to Italian law and regulation. What to watch next is the tender's progress toward that December deadline and any CONSOB or Italian government filings along the way.
